unit.label: Restaurants, cooking & learning
unit.title: Spicy Food & Cooking Skills
unit.description: 13 new words and forms. Talk about yesterday, react to spicy food, explain a choice, and describe cooking skills.

goal.pinyin: Wǒ huì zuòfàn, yě zuò de búcuò.
goal.meaning: I can cook, and I do it pretty well.

unit.bookReference: A Course in Contemporary Chinese 1 · Lesson 5 牛肉麵真好吃 · pp. 89–95, 99.

lessons.title: Yesterday at a Restaurant
lessons.subtitle: Name the place, say when, and add a contrasting comment.

steps.prompt: Which means yesterday?
steps.explanation: 昨天 is the day before 今天; 明天 is the day after.

steps.prompt: Choose the measure word: 兩＿＿餐廳。
steps.explanation: 家 counts restaurants, 碗 counts bowls, and 支 counts phones in the earlier lesson.

steps.prompt: The food tastes good, but it is expensive. Choose the connector.
steps.explanation: 可是 links the contrasting comments 好吃 and 貴.
昨 is read zuó. Choose the character matching the spoken syllable.

lessons.title: A Little Spicy
lessons.subtitle: Separate spice from temperature and explain your tolerance.

steps.prompt: Which comment means a little spicy?
steps.explanation: 有一點辣 is a mild spice warning. 很熱 is about temperature, and 不辣 means not spicy.

steps.prompt: A diner says 我不怕辣. What do you know?
options: Spicy food does not bother them.
Spicy food is definitely their favorite.
steps.answer: Spicy food does not bother them.
steps.explanation: 不怕辣 tells you about tolerance, without claiming a favorite.
辣 is read là. Choose the character matching the spoken syllable.

lessons.title: So I Cook Myself
lessons.subtitle: Give a result and describe doing the cooking yourself.

steps.prompt: Complete the result: 我怕辣，＿＿我想吃不辣的麵。
steps.explanation: 所以 introduces the choice resulting from being sensitive to spicy food.

steps.prompt: What does 我自己做飯 tell you?
options: I am the only person in the house.
steps.explanation: 自己 emphasizes the person doing the action. 做飯 means preparing a meal.

steps.prompt: Which character completes the word zìjǐ, oneself? 自＿＿
steps.explanation: 自己 uses 己. 幾 has the same jǐ reading but asks how many.

lessons.title: Desserts & Compliments
lessons.subtitle: Build 甜點 and give a positive reaction.

steps.prompt: Someone tastes dessert and says 不錯. What do they mean?
steps.explanation: 不錯 is a positive quality comment in this context.

steps.prompt: Which means make desserts?
steps.explanation: 做甜點 uses 做 for making; 吃甜點 means eat desserts.
甜 is read tián. Choose the character matching the spoken syllable.

lessons.title: How Well Do You Cook?
lessons.subtitle: Use 得, keep the object in the right place, and ask about performance.

steps.prompt: Choose the correctly placed 得.
steps.explanation: With 飯 after 做, repeat 做 before 得: 做飯做得很好.

steps.prompt: Which says the cooking is not done well?
steps.explanation: 做得不好 evaluates the performance. 不做飯 denies the activity; 不想做飯 denies wanting it.

steps.prompt: Which character links 做 to 很好 in this performance comment? 做＿＿很好。
steps.explanation: 得 follows an action verb and introduces its performance description.

steps.prompt: Choose the neutral reading of 得 in 做得很好.
steps.explanation: The performance marker is neutral-tone de, as taught on its grammar card.

lessons.title: Could You Teach Me?
lessons.subtitle: Ask for help and separate knowing how from doing it well.

steps.prompt: Choose the reading of 教 when you ask someone to teach you.
steps.explanation: The teaching verb in 教我 is first-tone jiāo. Other readings belong to other uses.

steps.prompt: You want to ask whether someone knows how to cook. Choose the question.
steps.explanation: 會 asks about having the learned skill. 得怎麼樣 asks how well it is done.

steps.prompt: Who is learning in 我姐姐教我做甜點？
steps.explanation: 我姐姐 is the teacher; 我 after 教 is the learner.

lessons.title: Restaurant & Cooking Review
lessons.subtitle: Use the complete unit in a meal-and-learning conversation.

steps.prompt: The soup is a little spicy, but tastes good. Choose the matching comment.
options: 湯有一點辣，可是很好喝。
steps.answer: 湯有一點辣，可是很好喝。
steps.explanation: 有一點辣 gives the mild drawback; 可是 introduces the favorable contrast.

steps.prompt: Complete the performance pattern: 我做甜點＿＿很好。
steps.explanation: After 做甜點, repeat 做 before 得 and the description.

steps.prompt: Review: choose the total for a 130-dollar bowl and a 40-dollar dessert.
Review: you want two bowls of noodles. Choose the order.
steps.explanation: 碗 counts portions served in bowls; 家 counts establishments and 支 counts phones here.

newVocabulary.meaning: fear; dislike or be sensitive to
marker linking a verb to a description of its performance
newVocabulary.note: New grammar use of the character already taught in 覺得.

昨.note: 昨 combines with the familiar 天 to make 昨天, yesterday. Keep its rising second tone distinct from 做 zuò.
昨.memory: The narrow 日 stands beside 乍, whose two short inner lines sit below the top cross.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: left sun component
parts.description: Write the narrow four-stroke 日 on the left.

parts.label: 乍
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Start with the short slant and upper horizontal, then the vertical and two shorter horizontals beneath it.

餐.note: 餐 begins 餐廳, restaurant. Read cān with a level first tone; the word names a place to eat.
餐.memory: The seven strokes at the top sit over a broad 食, the food component.

parts.label: 𣦼
parts.name: upper seven-stroke group
parts.description: Write the small upper-left group first, followed by the two crossing strokes of 又 on its right.

parts.label: 食
parts.name: lower food component
parts.description: Begin 食 with its spreading roof, then build the box and finish its descending lower strokes. Keep this nine-stroke component centered below the top group.

廳.meaning: hall; final syllable of 餐廳
廳.note: 廳 completes 餐廳, restaurant. Its tīng sounds like the familiar 聽; the enclosing roof distinguishes this written character.
廳.memory: A wide 广 roof shelters an ear on the left and a heart at the lower right.

parts.label: 广
parts.name: outer roof
parts.description: Write the dot, broad roof line and long left-falling stroke first.

parts.label: 耳
parts.name: inner upper-left ear
parts.description: Inside the roof, write the top horizontal, left vertical and long right vertical before the inner horizontals and lower rising line.

parts.label: 壬
parts.name: inner lower-left group
parts.description: Below the ear, write the short slanting top line, central vertical, middle horizontal and lower rising line.

parts.label: 十罒一心
parts.name: right-hand stack
parts.description: Work downward through the cross, five-stroke flat eye shape and horizontal line, then finish 心 with its left dot, bent hook and two remaining dots.

辣.note: 辣 describes the peppery heat of food. 熱 describes temperature, so food can be 熱 without being 辣.
辣.memory: 辛 has a long descending last stroke on the left; 束 keeps a box around its central line on the right.

parts.label: 辛
parts.name: left component
parts.description: Write the dot, horizontal and two small inward strokes, then two horizontals and the long descending left-falling stroke.

parts.label: 束
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write the top horizontal and central box, then the long central vertical and the two spreading lower strokes.

怕.meaning: fear; dislike or be sensitive to
怕.note: 怕 means fear or be afraid of. In 怕辣 it describes someone who dislikes or cannot comfortably tolerate spicy food.
怕.memory: The slim heart component 忄 stands beside a compact white 白.

parts.label: 忄
parts.name: left heart component
parts.description: Write the left dot and right dot, then the longer vertical between them.

parts.label: 白
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Start with the short top slant, then write the upright box with its inner horizontal and closing base.

example.meaning: dislike or be sensitive to spicy food

所.meaning: first syllable of 所以, so
所.note: Learn 所以 as the complete connector meaning so or therefore. 所 by itself is not the connector in this lesson.
所.memory: A small 戶 sits to the left of 斤, with two long downward strokes keeping the halves apart.

parts.label: 戶
parts.name: left component
parts.description: Start with the slanted top stroke, the bent upper shape and its horizontal, then the long left-falling stroke.

parts.label: 斤
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write the upper slant and longer left-falling stroke, then the horizontal and final vertical.

自.note: 自 begins 自己, oneself. In 我自己做飯, the person doing the cooking is me.
自.memory: A small top slant rests on a tall box with two inner horizontal lines.

parts.label: 丿
parts.name: top slant
parts.description: Write the short left-falling stroke above the box.

parts.label: 目
parts.name: lower box
parts.description: Write the left side, top-and-right bend, two inner horizontals and closing bottom horizontal.

己.note: 己 completes 自己. Its third-tone jǐ differs from the familiar 幾 jǐ in writing even though they sound alike.
己.memory: The upper corner bends down to a middle shelf; the last stroke curls underneath without closing the upper opening.

parts.label: 己
parts.name: three-stroke curled structure
parts.description: Write the top horizontal-and-downward bend, then the middle horizontal. Finish with the long curved stroke below, keeping its upper end below the top edge.

甜.note: 甜 gives 甜點 its sweet-food meaning. The familiar 點 has a new role inside this whole word; it is not the ordering verb here.
甜.memory: 舌 fills the left half; the compact 甘 on the right has an extra horizontal inside its open-topped shape.

parts.label: 舌
parts.name: left tongue component
parts.description: Write the top slant, horizontal and vertical, then the three-stroke 口 beneath.

parts.label: 甘
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write the upper horizontal, left and right verticals, inner horizontal and bottom horizontal.

錯.meaning: wrong; in 不錯, not bad
錯.note: 錯 can mean wrong. The complete expression 不錯 means not bad or pretty good; do not translate every use as not mistaken.
錯.memory: The metal component 金 is on the left; 昔 puts a wide cross-shaped top above 日 on the right.

parts.label: 金
parts.name: left metal component
parts.description: Write the spreading top, two horizontals and central vertical, then its two small lower marks and final rising base.

parts.label: 昔
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Write the upper horizontal, two verticals and lower horizontal, then the four-stroke 日 underneath.

教.note: For the verb teach in 教我, use first-tone jiāo. The character also has a jiào reading in other words; those uses are outside this lesson.
教.memory: 孝 fills the left side, with a small 子 beneath its crossed top; 攵 sends two long strokes across the right.

parts.label: 孝
parts.name: left component
parts.description: Write the horizontal, vertical, second horizontal and descending slant, then the three strokes of 子 below.

parts.label: 攵
parts.name: right action component
parts.description: Write the short slant and horizontal, followed by the longer left-falling and right-falling strokes.

u16-yesterday.title: Place yesterday before the action
u16-yesterday.pattern: subject + 昨天 + action; 昨天 + subject + action
u16-yesterday.explanation: 昨天 means yesterday, the day before today. Like 今天 and 明天, it goes before the action. Chinese verbs do not change their spelling for yesterday; this sentence does not need an automatic past-tense 了.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān zài jiā.
examples.meaning: I was at home yesterday.

examples.pinyin: Zuótiān wǎnshàng wǒ kàn diànyǐng.
examples.meaning: I watched a movie last night.

u16-yesterday.remember: 昨天 is yesterday; 明天 is tomorrow. The time phrase supplies the time.

u16-restaurant.title: Count restaurants with the familiar 家
u16-restaurant.pattern: 這 / 那 / number + 家 + 餐廳
u16-restaurant.explanation: 餐廳 means restaurant. Use 家 to count restaurants just as you used it for shops. 這家餐廳 means this restaurant; 兩家餐廳 means two restaurants.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān qù nà jiā cāntīng.
examples.meaning: I went to that restaurant yesterday.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng hěn yǒumíng.
examples.meaning: This restaurant is well-known.

u16-restaurant.remember: 家 counts the establishment; 碗 counts bowls of food.

u16-contrast.title: Connect two contrasting comments
u16-contrast.pattern: first statement + 可是 + contrasting statement
u16-contrast.explanation: 可是 means but or however. Put it between two statements that contrast. 和 joins nouns in earlier lessons; it does not replace 可是 when you mean but.

examples.text: 這家餐廳的菜很好吃，可是很貴。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài hěn hǎochī, kěshì hěn guì.
examples.meaning: The food at this restaurant is delicious, but expensive.

examples.text: 我想去，可是我媽媽不想去。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù, kěshì wǒ māma bù xiǎng qù.
examples.meaning: I want to go, but my mom does not.

u16-contrast.remember: 可是 introduces the contrasting comment. The subject can be left out when it is still clear.

u16-spicy.title: Spice is different from temperature
u16-spicy.explanation: 辣 means spicy, the peppery heat of food. 熱 is hot in temperature. 不辣 means not spicy; it does not say the food is cold.

examples.pinyin: Zhè wǎn miàn hěn là.
examples.meaning: This bowl of noodles is spicy.

examples.pinyin: Tāng hěn rè, kěshì bú là.
examples.meaning: The soup is hot, but not spicy.

u16-spicy.remember: Use 辣 for spice and 熱 for temperature.

u16-a-little.title: Give a mild criticism
u16-a-little.explanation: 有一點 means a little or somewhat before a description. Here it presents a mild drawback: 有一點辣, a little spicy, or 有一點貴, a little expensive. It is not an extra 很 and is not the default way to praise delicious food. Use 很好吃 or 真好吃 for that. The 一 is spoken yì before 點 diǎn.

examples.pinyin: Zhè wǎn tāng yǒu yìdiǎn là.
examples.meaning: This bowl of soup is a little spicy.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng yǒu yìdiǎn guì.
examples.meaning: This restaurant is a little expensive.

u16-a-little.remember: 有一點 goes before the description. In this lesson it softens a complaint.

u16-sensitive.title: Say you are sensitive to spicy food
u16-sensitive.explanation: 怕 means fear or be afraid of. In 怕辣 it means you dislike or cannot comfortably tolerate spicy food. 不怕辣 means you are not bothered by spicy food; it does not necessarily mean spicy food is your favorite.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ pà là.
examples.meaning: I am sensitive to spicy food.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiějie bú pà là.
examples.meaning: My older sister is not bothered by spicy food.

u16-sensitive.remember: 怕辣 describes the person’s tolerance; 很辣 describes the food.

u16-result.title: Put the reason first and the result second
u16-result.explanation: 所以 means so or therefore. State the reason, then use 所以 to introduce what follows from it. You can use this pattern on its own; no extra word is required before the reason.

examples.text: 我怕辣，所以我不想吃這碗麵。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ pà là, suǒyǐ wǒ bù xiǎng chī zhè wǎn miàn.
examples.meaning: I am sensitive to spicy food, so I do not want to eat this bowl of noodles.

examples.text: 這家餐廳很有名，所以很多人想去。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng hěn yǒumíng, suǒyǐ hěn duō rén xiǎng qù.
examples.meaning: This restaurant is famous, so many people want to go.

u16-result.remember: 所以 introduces a result. 可是 introduces a contrast.

u16-cook-yourself.title: Use 自己 before the action
u16-cook-yourself.explanation: 自己 means oneself. 做飯 is the everyday expression for cooking or preparing a meal; it is not limited to cooking rice. 我自己做飯 says I do the cooking myself. It does not by itself mean nobody else is in the house.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ cháng zìjǐ zuòfàn.
examples.meaning: I often do the cooking myself.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ māma xǐhuān zìjǐ zuòfàn.
examples.meaning: My mom likes to cook herself.

u16-cook-yourself.remember: 自己 goes before the action it emphasizes; 做飯 names the activity.

u16-dessert.title: Use the whole word 甜點
u16-dessert.explanation: 甜點 means dessert or a sweet dish. 甜 contributes the idea sweet; 點 is part of the food word here. 做甜點 means make desserts. The earlier verb 點 still means order in 點一碗麵, so read the whole expression.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuān chī tiándiǎn.
examples.meaning: I like eating desserts most.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiějie xǐhuān zuò tiándiǎn.
examples.meaning: My older sister likes making desserts.

u16-dessert.remember: 點 is part of 甜點; do not translate 甜點 as sweet order.

u16-not-bad.title: Give a modest positive comment
u16-not-bad.explanation: 不錯 is the everyday positive expression not bad or pretty good. It can describe food or other things. Although 錯 can mean wrong, 不錯 here is a compliment about quality. 不 changes to second-tone bú before fourth-tone cuò.

examples.text: 這家餐廳的甜點很不錯。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de tiándiǎn hěn búcuò.
examples.meaning: This restaurant’s desserts are pretty good.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ juéde zhè wǎn miàn búcuò.
examples.meaning: I think this bowl of noodles is pretty good.

u16-not-bad.remember: 不錯 is positive in these food comments; 不好吃 is negative.

u16-performance.title: Describe how an action is done
u16-performance.explanation: 得 after a verb links the action to a description of how it is done: 做得很好, do it well. Its reading here is neutral-tone de. It is a separate grammar use of the character you met in 覺得. It is not the 的 used for possession or before an understood noun.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuò de hěn hǎo.
examples.meaning: You do it very well.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuò de búcuò.
examples.meaning: I do it pretty well.

u16-performance.remember: Put 得 directly after the action verb, then describe the performance.

u16-object-repeat.title: Repeat the verb after its object
u16-object-repeat.pattern: verb + object + same verb + 得 + description
u16-object-repeat.explanation: If you keep an object immediately after the action verb, repeat the verb before 得. 做飯 becomes 做飯做得很好. 做甜點 becomes 做甜點做得不錯. If the object is understood, you can simply say 做得很好.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiějie zuòfàn zuò de hěn hǎo.
examples.meaning: My older sister cooks very well.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuò tiándiǎn zuò de búcuò.
examples.meaning: I make desserts pretty well.

u16-object-repeat.remember: 得 follows the repeated verb, not the object 飯 or 甜點.

u16-object-first.title: Put the topic first instead
u16-object-first.pattern: object as topic + ，person + verb + 得 + description
u16-object-first.explanation: You can put the object at the front as the topic. Then say the person, the verb, 得 and the description. Since the object is no longer after the verb, there is no need to repeat the verb.

examples.pinyin: Tiándiǎn, wǒ jiějie zuò de hěn hǎo.
examples.meaning: As for desserts, my older sister makes them very well.

examples.pinyin: Zhōngwén, wǒ shuō de búcuò.
examples.meaning: As for Chinese, I speak it pretty well.

u16-object-first.remember: Compare 我做甜點做得很好 with 甜點，我做得很好. Both keep 得 directly after 做.

u16-performance-questions.title: Ask how well, or say not well
u16-performance-questions.pattern: verb + 得 + 怎麼樣 / 好不好？; verb + 得 + 不好
u16-performance-questions.explanation: 怎麼樣 after 得 asks how well the action is done. 好不好 can ask whether it is done well. For a negative performance comment, put 不 inside the description after 得: 做得不好. This evaluates the performance; 我不做飯 instead says I do not cook.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuòfàn zuò de zěnmeyàng?
examples.meaning: How well do you cook?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuò de hǎo bu hǎo?
examples.meaning: Do you do it well?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuò de bù hǎo.
examples.meaning: I do not do it well.

u16-performance-questions.remember: Ask 做得怎麼樣; answer 做得很好 / 不錯 / 不好.

u16-teach.title: Name the teacher, learner and skill
u16-teach.explanation: 教 means teach and is jiāo, first tone, in this use. Put the learner after 教, followed by what is taught when needed. 教我做飯 means teach me to cook; 教我中文 means teach me Chinese. When the activity is already clear, 教我 is enough.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiějie jiāo wǒ zuò tiándiǎn.
examples.meaning: My older sister teaches me to make desserts.

examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī jiāo wǒmen Zhōngwén.
examples.meaning: The teacher teaches us Chinese.

u16-teach.remember: Teach someone: 教 + person + activity or language.

u16-teaching-request.title: Ask whether someone could teach you
u16-teaching-request.pattern: 你 + 可以 + 教 + 我 + activity + 嗎？
u16-teaching-request.explanation: Use 可以 to ask if it is possible for someone to teach you. In this direct request, 你可以教我…嗎？ is a polite Could you teach me…? If the skill is already clear, 你可以教我嗎？ works too.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ jiāo wǒ zuòfàn ma?
examples.meaning: Could you teach me to cook?

examples.text: 我想學做甜點，你可以教我嗎？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xué zuò tiándiǎn, nǐ kěyǐ jiāo wǒ ma?
examples.meaning: I want to learn to make desserts. Could you teach me?

u16-teaching-request.remember: 可以 asks whether the help is possible; 教 names the teaching action.

u16-skill-performance.title: Knowing how and doing it well are different
u16-skill-performance.pattern: 會 + activity; verb + 得 + performance
u16-skill-performance.explanation: Review 會 for a skill learned through practice. 你會做飯嗎？ asks whether you know how to cook. 你做飯做得怎麼樣？ asks how well you cook. Someone can know how without doing it well yet.

examples.text: 我會做飯，可是做得不好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ huì zuòfàn, kěshì zuò de bù hǎo.
examples.meaning: I know how to cook, but I do not do it well.

examples.text: 我會做甜點，也做得不錯。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ huì zuò tiándiǎn, yě zuò de búcuò.
examples.meaning: I can make desserts, and I make them pretty well.

u16-skill-performance.remember: 會 asks about learned ability; 得 introduces an evaluation of performance.

u16-yesterday-meal.text: 我昨天晚上去那家餐廳吃晚飯。
u16-yesterday-meal.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān wǎnshàng qù nà jiā cāntīng chī wǎnfàn.
u16-yesterday-meal.meaning: I went to that restaurant for dinner last night.

u16-restaurant-contrast.text: 那家餐廳很有名，可是菜很貴。
u16-restaurant-contrast.pinyin: Nà jiā cāntīng hěn yǒumíng, kěshì cài hěn guì.
u16-restaurant-contrast.meaning: That restaurant is famous, but the food is expensive.

u16-spicy-noodles.text: 這碗牛肉麵很好吃，可是有一點辣。
u16-spicy-noodles.pinyin: Zhè wǎn niúròu miàn hěn hǎochī, kěshì yǒu yìdiǎn là.
u16-spicy-noodles.meaning: This bowl of beef noodles is delicious, but a little spicy.

u16-not-spicy-choice.text: 我怕辣，我想點不辣的麵。
u16-not-spicy-choice.pinyin: Wǒ pà là, wǒ xiǎng diǎn bú là de miàn.
u16-not-spicy-choice.meaning: I am sensitive to spicy food. I want to order noodles that are not spicy.

u16-cook-reason.text: 我怕辣，所以我喜歡自己做飯。
u16-cook-reason.pinyin: Wǒ pà là, suǒyǐ wǒ xǐhuān zìjǐ zuòfàn.
u16-cook-reason.meaning: I am sensitive to spicy food, so I like to cook myself.

u16-yesterday-cook.text: 我昨天晚上在家自己做飯。
u16-yesterday-cook.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān wǎnshàng zài jiā zìjǐ zuòfàn.
u16-yesterday-cook.meaning: I cooked at home myself last night.
u16-yesterday-cook.note: 在家 locates the cooking at home. 自己 says who does it.

u16-dessert-choice.text: 我最喜歡這家餐廳的甜點。
u16-dessert-choice.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuān zhè jiā cāntīng de tiándiǎn.
u16-dessert-choice.meaning: I like this restaurant’s desserts most.

u16-dessert-comment.text: 這家餐廳的菜有一點貴，可是甜點很不錯。
u16-dessert-comment.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài yǒu yìdiǎn guì, kěshì tiándiǎn hěn búcuò.
u16-dessert-comment.meaning: This restaurant’s food is a little expensive, but the desserts are pretty good.

u16-making-desserts-well.pinyin: Wǒ zuò tiándiǎn zuò de hěn hǎo.

u16-dessert-topic.meaning: As for desserts, I make them pretty well.

u16-teach-desserts.text: 我想學做甜點，你可以教我嗎？
u16-teach-desserts.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xué zuò tiándiǎn, nǐ kěyǐ jiāo wǒ ma?
u16-teach-desserts.meaning: I want to learn to make desserts. Could you teach me?

u16-can-but-not-well.text: 我會做飯，可是做得不好。
u16-can-but-not-well.pinyin: Wǒ huì zuòfàn, kěshì zuò de bù hǎo.
u16-can-but-not-well.meaning: I can cook, but I do not do it well.

u16-review-restaurant.text: 昨天晚上我去那家餐廳吃麵。
u16-review-restaurant.pinyin: Zuótiān wǎnshàng wǒ qù nà jiā cāntīng chī miàn.
u16-review-restaurant.meaning: I went to that restaurant for noodles last night.

u16-review-reason.text: 我怕辣，所以常自己做飯。
u16-review-reason.pinyin: Wǒ pà là, suǒyǐ cháng zìjǐ zuòfàn.
u16-review-reason.meaning: I am sensitive to spicy food, so I often cook myself.

u16-review-goal.pinyin: Wǒ huì zuòfàn, yě zuò de búcuò.
u16-review-goal.meaning: I can cook, and I do it pretty well.

u16-review-teach.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ jiāo wǒ zuò tiándiǎn ma?
u16-review-teach.meaning: Could you teach me to make desserts?
